assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the five REVIEWED items curated on shokugeki-no-soma:yukihira-soma@manga at basis_commit, each read in full for this assessment: #reviewed-dedicated-analysis, the canonical V2 full-series character model (SHOKUGEKI_SOMA_V2_FULL_SERIES_CHARACTER_MODEL.md, readiness validated_model) consolidated from the project's complete original-Japanese V01-V36 sequential reread including Le dessert; #soma-final-character-model, the canonical V1 final model built from the sampled volumes V01, V03, V08, V13, V19 and V25 with V30 and V36 as prospective holdouts; #soma-model-validation-audit, the canonical V1 audit of those holdouts (V30 9 CONFIRM / 1 PARTIAL, V36 9 CONFIRM / 1 UNTESTED) and its threats to validity; and the active_provisional V1 #soma-behavioral-model-ledger and #soma-japanese-voice-ledger over the same eight sampled volumes. All five derive from one project and are one line of evidence, not independent corroboration; the V1 holdout scoring was performed by the same process that built the model. The project's readiness labels, its validated_model status and the audit's authority statement are inputs, not conclusions. The full-series deep readings, character-state, ensemble-voice, relationship and readiness ledgers, evidence matrix, the V2 full-series validation audit and the V2 reconstruction-fidelity audit that the V2 model routes to are not curated on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. Anime, audio performance, supplementary comics beyond their stated low weight, other characters' models and anything after the Le dessert 3 Futur epilogue are out of scope; the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Yukihira Soma from the remembered childhood Yukihira years (Tamako's cooking and death, Joichiro's 490 wins, the childhood delivery to an injured regular) through the Le dessert 3 Futur age-25 return (36-224 to 36-243), under the V2 model's five developmental states: diner son and academy entrant V01-V04; learner among independent rivals V05-V14; coalition cook V15-V30; First Seat and BLUE competitor V31-V36 serialized (ending at 36-145); and the adult return in Futur. Présent, Passé and Futur are separate states and are never projected back onto the serialized chapters, and the V30 final course and its V31 process objection (31-006 to 31-012) are distinct states. This boundary limits which evidence is used, not what he knows: Tamako's failure culture and his mother's death belong to him at every state they predate even though their disclosure is in V36. With no time specified the default is the terminal adult working cook, whose routines, legal ownership of Yukihira and romantic status are not established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits and relationship-transfer safeguards); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: A discriminating operational model: the V2 thesis (low defensiveness toward actionable evidence) with seven stable rules, competing priorities stated as tendencies, and an eleven-row conditional decision policy with exceptions and H/M/U warrants; the V1 model's conditional rules and scenario variables (actionability, credibility of the adverse judgment, kind of authority, the other person's competence or vulnerability, relationship, prestige versus function). It says which consideration decides: a credible fair loss is approached while an evidence-inconsistent or procedurally illegitimate verdict is contested (SBR-012); local task authority is obeyed while permanent role capture is refused (Tsukasa, V19-V20; Erina, V30). It predicts his mistakes: overreading reluctance as a challengeable barrier (Kanon, 08-067 to 08-085), assuming a challenge that energizes him energizes others, overestimating the legitimacy of extreme stakes (Mimasaka), and overrunning consultation (31-006 to 31-012). The V1 rules survived two frozen holdouts with no MISS. Not A: the holdouts were scored by the process that built the model, are strategic, broad and correlated, and cannot exclude latent series knowledge (audit section 15); the V2 motive ordering is explicitly not lexicographic. Not C: the evidence does more than interpret; it supplies the discriminating account and states where it stops.

Five developmental states with available behavior and transfer gates (V01-V04, V05-V14, V15-V30, V31-V36, Futur) and per-arc movements with locators (Shinomiya 03-060 to 04-143, Mimasaka 10-130 to 11-153, SHINO'S 13-043 to 14-183, Moon Festival 15-006 to 16-148, Tsukasa 19-088 to 20-086, final course 30-021 to 30-184, Asahi 32-048 to 32-098 and 35-139 to 36-075). The gates forbid retrofitting mature calibration into the V01 entrance speech and forbid letting office imply best-in-every-task. The V1 ledger records claim transitions volume by volume with frozen predictions before V30 and V36. Not A: the states are multi-volume bands, the V1 ledgers cover eight sampled volumes and the behavioral ledger lacks its V19 transition section, and the adult state is underdescribed. Not C: located state changes and gates are explicit.

A Japanese register model with recipient-specific rules and located forms: 俺 default, 親父, ウチ; casual contractions; shallow ～っす accommodation with 先輩 carrying blunt disagreement (納得いかないっすね, 03; 司先輩, 30-054 to 30-064); compressed task acceptance 合点 (30-079 to 30-083, 30-115 to 30-117); service markers おあがりよ and 御粗末 tied to presenting and closing; dry deflation (よかったね おめでとう); plain diction for serious content (積み上げてきた時間がね, 25-081); unchanged familiar register at age 25 (36-232 to 36-235). The voice ledger's frozen tests returned 8 CONFIRM at V30 and confirmed at V36. Not A: there is no frequency census, the voice ledger omits its V08, V13 and V19 sections (numbering jumps from section 17 to 53 while later tables cite SV-011 and SV-012), the V1 model's example lines are labeled synthetic, and timing, pitch and actor delivery are outside the manga warrant. Not C: the register rules discriminate by recipient and survived prospective holdouts.

The V2 ordinary-life table gives observed surfaces with bounded inference: low-ceremony food play and strange experiments, group tables after unequal results, the childhood delivery to an injured regular with minimized gesture (08-162 to 08-168), frustration such as the wall strike after the camp defeat, unglamorous routine kitchen work, and adult travel with intermittent communication. Food remains the dominant interface (SBR-015). The audit rates everyday intimacy outside the culinary ecosystem MEDIUM/OPEN (16.8) and the V2 model leaves adult emotional routines and domestic arrangements underdescribed. Not B: outside food-anchored settings the evidence does not say what decides his ordinary conduct. Not D: food-anchored ordinary behavior is described with located observations and limits.

Recipient-specific models for Erina, Megumi, Joichiro, Tamako, Hayama, Takumi, Alice, Nene, Tsukasa, Shinomiya, Hisako, ordinary customers and children, with a competence-and-vulnerability variable: real tasks and named credit for an anxious capable peer, consequence reduction for a shame-fragile novice after provocation misfires, a practical bridge for Hisako (13-150 to 13-160), and hard challenge for a highly capable under-authoring peer (Erina, V30 and 36-099 to 36-134). The V2 model warns that the same provocation toward an unknown frightened first-year lacks relational warrant and that the V30 provocation still drew Erina's V31 objection. Holdouts confirmed relationship non-totalization at V30 and V36; the V30 care test was PARTIAL. Not A: Erina's romantic status, transfer to unsampled relations and repeated refused emotional support are not established. Not C: the variation is explained by stated mechanisms, not only described.

Emotion-to-action routing is stated for excitement, envy, frustration, affection, embarrassment, anger at dispossession and grief, each tied to separate scenes, and the V1 model preserves real nervousness, disappointment and sustained reflection after the V13 loss (SBR-010). Interior states are inferred from behavior and from his tendency to state the next attempt rather than a feeling; grief is shown through shared cooking after Tamako's funeral, not a bereavement theory, and the V2 model calls its confidence scene-specific rather than a transferable resilience score. Not B: the evidence does not give a demonstrated interior model that predicts unshown affect. Not D: a structured routing account with locators exists.

Typed losses (3-0 technical defeat, tournament placement, private loss, bad dish) change practice without universal inferiority; illegitimate judgment is contested through an adjudicative mechanism (Shinomiya, V03; Central, V19); rivals are approached after both defeat (13-053) and victory (25-116); the failure-distinction table separates prototype, buffet system, ballot, brigade action and flawed intervention, the last not repaired by a winning dish. Mistakes are modeled: extreme stakes against Mimasaka, unsolicited provocation exceeding consent, the V31 objection. Not A: intimate conflict that cooking cannot mediate, third-party mediation and non-culinary physical danger are open (audit 16.2, model 21.3). Not C: the evidence discriminates which response follows which conflict type.

Located ethical positions: culinary pluralism against Central's erasure of ordinary restaurants (V19), returning all 99 tools rather than enforcing vocational annihilation (10-130 to 11-153), recognizing that the owner decides a restaurant's direction (SBR-026, V13), refusing authority over another person through a stake, and failure tolerance that is not consent to serving harmful experiments. The evidence frames these as concrete consequences, not a deliberation procedure; the audit rates non-food ideological disputes MEDIUM/OPEN and leaves deep apology after serious harm and deception underdetermined (16.5-16.7). Not B: outside culinary and institutional frames the evidence does not say how competing values are weighed. Not D: the positions are located and consistent across volumes.

Humor functions are described: bizarre dishes, blunt speech and bodily comedy keep risk survivable (rule 7), teasing is aimed at a particular recipient and must be justified after a misfire, dry deflation answers overperformed rivalry (SV-008), playful ritual invitation pulls a peer into group affect (25-127 to 25-128, SV-023 medium), and the age-25 bad dish is met with amusement (36-237 to 36-242). The model warns that humor can ignore discomfort or overrun another person's timing, with the Kanon misfire as the located case. Not B: beyond teasing and failed-food play no comic repertoire, timing or choice of when to joke is modeled. Not D: the functions and their limits are located.

The V2 model is a consolidation of the project's complete original-Japanese V01-V36 sequential reread, including Le dessert, with archive-image locators across the series and stated exclusions of defective or obscured images; the V1 artifacts sample eight volumes with V30 and V36 held out and say so. Not A: the V2 model was consolidated through analytical retrieval from deep readings and validation audits that are not curated on this subject, both V1 ledgers visibly omit middle sections, and the evaluator inspected no primary source. Not C: full-series coverage, not a sample, underlies the current model.

Affirmative limits and contradictions are recorded: he can overstep consultation (31-006 to 31-012); he is not best in every comparison (Erina wins BLUE; Asahi, Tsukasa and Hayama defeat him); he is not documented as Yukihira's legal owner; he does not receive Erina's verdict; explicit romance is not established; his first engagement strategy misfires on concealed shame (Kanon, V08). Negative controls and anti-archetype corrections exclude the invincible prodigy, anti-elite populist, lone genius and always-leader readings, and the audit preserves the V30 PARTIAL and V36 UNTESTED instead of normalizing them. Not A: these are the project's own limits, not independently audited. Not C: they are specific, located and consequential for use.

Volume and archive-image locators (VV-NNN) bind claims; the state table gates transfer between periods; Présent, Passé and Futur stay separate from the serialized ending; the audit tiers V36 into serialized Chapters 309-315 ending at 36-145 and Le dessert, and forbids backward projection; earlier sequential readings are not rewritten with later knowledge. Not A: states are multi-volume bands and the adult state is thin. Not C: chronology is explicit and enforced.

conditions: Output is labeled illustrative and noncanonical; any line presented as canon is a located form, rechecked against its locator.
Japanese text and register only, or a translation that preserves speech act and register; no pitch, timing, accent or actor performance.

Register follows the recipient and state: 俺 baseline, 先輩 plus shallow ～っす with seniors and evaluators, plain teasing and challenge with Erina and peers, 親父 with Joichiro, conventional service formulas with customers; おあがりよ and 御粗末 only when presenting or closing food.
No polished romantic confession, therapeutic monologue, philosophical declaration, invented dialect or catchphrase attached to mundane exchanges.
scenario_readiness.note: The register rules constrain generated speech enough for illustrative use: recipient-specific forms, 先輩 with ～っす over blunt content, compressed task language, plain diction for serious matters, service markers only when food is presented or closed, and continuity of register at age 25, all validated in two frozen voice holdouts. Not knowing the exact wording is productive uncertainty. Not READY: there is no frequency census, the voice ledger omits its V08-V19 sections, and audio performance is outside the warrant. Not NOT_READY: the audit's rule that generated lines are synthetic bounds use; it does not find output unsupported.

conditions: One named developmental state with that state's knowledge, under the transfer gates; the default terminal adult only when no time is given.
A sampled relationship class in its located standing; transfer to a comparable unsampled recipient is a separate, lower-confidence condition justified by the competence-and-vulnerability variable.
The output is a labeled range that keeps exceptions live: shame may be misread before it becomes legible, a challenge may overrun consent, and extreme stakes may be overvalued.
Abstain on precise adult schedule, legal ownership, named romantic agreements, Erina's unspoken answer, non-culinary expertise and guaranteed competitive outcomes.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named V2 developmental state (V01-V04 entrant, V05-V14 learner, V15-V30 coalition cook, V31-V36 First Seat and BLUE competitor ending at 36-145, or the Le dessert 3 Futur adult), with the V30 final course and the V31 objection treated as distinct moments; Tamako's culture and death count as his knowledge throughout; nothing after Futur.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Sampled relationship classes in their located standing: Erina as rival, evaluator, collaborator and privileged recipient without established romance; Megumi as capable peer; Joichiro as familial benchmark; Takumi, Hayama, Alice, Nene and Tsukasa as rivals or senior experts; Hisako as shame-blocked peer; Shinomiya as challengeable senior; customers and children. An unsampled recipient comparable to one of these is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Culinary, competitive, institutional-school, stagiaire, service and shared-kitchen settings the corpus samples
No medical, legal, financial or trauma expertise attributed to him
No life-threatening violence, disaster response or non-culinary crisis
No established romance, marriage, legal ownership of Yukihira or guaranteed outcome in an unseen competition

scenario_readiness.note: The V2 conditional policy, the V1 scenario variables and the noncanonical probes support bounded extrapolation that keeps his characteristic mistakes live (misreading shame, overrunning consent, risky stakes). Not READY: transfer outside the sampled settings and relationships is unvalidated and the holdout validation is same-process. Not NOT_READY: the model specifies inputs, exceptions and abstentions for novel situations.

conditions: Food-anchored ordinary settings with sampled relationships: shared tables, tasting, experiments, teasing and routine kitchen work.
Competition may continue inside belonging, but not every conversation becomes a challenge.
Adult domestic routines, sustained cohabitation and non-food intimacy are not modeled; outputs there are labeled extrapolation or withheld.
scenario_readiness.note: Food-anchored downtime with familiar peers is described with bounded inference; quiet domestic conversation without a cooking or problem anchor is MEDIUM/OPEN in the audit. Not READY for that reason; not NOT_READY because the food-anchored baseline is located.

conditions: The dilemma can be made concrete in culinary, institutional or service terms: who loses a place, who bears the cost, who owns the decision.
His reasoning is rendered concretely, not as abstract political theory; risky stakes and overrunning consultation remain possible errors.
Non-culinary ideological disputes, long-term repair after serious harm he caused, and strategic deception are not modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Dilemmas that translate into craft, evidence, procedural legitimacy or concrete consequences have located positions (pluralism, tools returned, owner's decision, no authority through a stake). Not READY: non-food ideological disputes, serious-harm repair and deception are open or underdetermined. Not NOT_READY: the located positions are consistent and discriminating within their frame.

The evidence affirmatively withholds romance: Erina's significance is strong romantic implication and exclusive evaluative importance without confession, partnership or marriage (36-224 to 36-243); the V2 model forbids polished confession language and the audit rates developed couple behavior OPEN. The Erina rivalry, evaluation and collaboration relationship is covered under relationship conditioning and cross-scenario use, not as romance. Not CONDITIONAL: no romance-specific behavior is established to condition on.

conditions: Culinary professional settings: service, competition, stagiaire work, shared courses and public operations, with local task authority following problem ownership.
He can be removed from a station and must regain usefulness; no automatic right to dictate the kitchen.
Long-duration brigade management, bureaucratic administration and adult client-facing register beyond the epilogue are not modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Kitchen, service, competition, stagiaire and shared-course work is the corpus's strongest domain, with the V30 dynamic-role sequence and the V13 system redesign. Not READY: long-duration management and adult client-facing register are open, and V36 did not retest interdependent hierarchy. Not NOT_READY: professional conduct is the best-evidenced domain.

known_limits.statement: Erina is a privileged evaluator and recipient with strong romantic implication, but no confession, partnership, marriage or achieved verdict is established; romantic scenes must not be generated as canon-consistent.
He loses under bounded conditions to Erina (BLUE), Asahi, Tsukasa, Hayama and others; office and endpoint status never imply culinary or interpersonal superiority.

His first engagement strategy can misfire on concealed shame (Kanon, 08-067 to 08-085); he recalibrates once the structure is legible, and a model must not grant him perfect access to hidden vulnerability.
He can overstep consultation, as Erina's post-Regiment process objection shows (31-006 to 31-012); a successful dish does not prove consent.
He may overestimate the legitimacy of extreme stakes (the Mimasaka career stake); model the risk rather than procedural infallibility.

The V1 holdouts were frozen in stored revisions but scored by the process that built the model, with strategic holdouts, broad correlated predictions and unexcluded latent series knowledge; the results are qualitative within-sample validation, not an accuracy rate.
Reversible task hierarchy in genuinely interdependent cooking rests on V30; V36 left it UNTESTED.

The behavioral ledger moves from its frozen V19 tests (section 11) to the V25 update (section 18) with no V19 transition, and the voice ledger moves from its V03 update (section 17) to V25 (section 53) with no V08, V13 or V19 sections; claims routed to those sections cannot be rechecked in this evidence set.
The V1 model's example Japanese lines are labeled illustrative reconstructions, and the audit requires generated dialogue to be labeled synthetic unless it is a verified located quotation.
Présent, Passé and Futur remain separate from the serialized ending, and later endpoint knowledge does not rewrite earlier publication-boundary states.
The adult return is a strong failure-response anchor but adult emotional routines, domestic arrangements, precise schedule and legal ownership of Yukihira are not established.
Present-time grief or bereavement behavior beyond shared cooking after Tamako's death is not established.
Behavior in life-threatening violence, disaster or other non-culinary physical danger is not established.
Long-duration formal people management, brigade command over months and bureaucratic administration are not established.
His response to months of exclusion from a field or team is not established.
A general policy for repeatedly refused emotional support where cooking is unwanted is not established.
Pitch, timing, accent and actor delivery are outside the manga warrant.
